title: Coaugmentation equation for the strict perfect-coefficient exchange
statement:
Let $S,T,X,Y$ be small ringed sites with a commutative square of ringed topoi $f:X\to S$, $g:T\to S$, $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$ and a specified ring-compatible isomorphism $fh\cong ge$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume all four coefficient pullbacks are isomorphisms, so module inverse images $L_u$ are exact, and use their canonical unbounded adjunctions $L_u\dashv R_u=Ru_*$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On $S$ fix a strict inverse sequence $Q_{S,\bullet}$ of complexes of coefficient modules, a strict augmentation $\Delta\mathcal O_S[0]\to Q_{S,\bullet}$, and assume every $Q_{S,n}$ is perfect, meaning locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite sums of $\mathcal O_S$. Pull this diagram to all other corners with the specified coefficient and square comparisons. On the small diagram sites [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] let $\mathcal R_W(M)=\Delta M\otimes^L Q_{W,\bullet}$, $\mathcal L_W=R\lim$, $C_W=\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_W$, and let $\kappa_{W,M}:M\to C_WM$ be the strict-augmentation map followed by derived inverse limit. Use the canonical constant-tower and evaluation comparisons preserving the ordinary derived adjunctions. They are the comparisons computed on K-injective towers, not choices of unrelated component isomorphisms.
For any $K\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ put $M=L_fR_gK$, $E=L_eK$, $N=R_hE$, and let $b:M\to N$ be the ordinary square mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Write $\mathscr L_u,\mathscr R_u$ for derived termwise inverse/direct image on the diagram sites, and put
$$B=\mathscr L_f\mathscr R_g\mathcal R_TK,\qquad D=\mathscr R_h\mathscr L_e\mathcal R_TK.$$
Let $H:\mathcal R_XM\to B$ and $H':\mathcal R_XN\to D$ be the projection-formula maps, meaning adjuncts of counit tensored with identity, including canonical pullback/tensor reassociation [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. These are invertible. Define
$$v=H'\mathcal R_X(b)H^{-1},\quad s=\mathcal L_XH:C_XM\to\mathcal L_XB,\quad c:R_hC_YE\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_XD,$$
where $c$ is the canonical derived-direct-image/derived-limit comparison whose projections are direct images of the tower projections. Then the natural morphism $\gamma_K=c^{-1}\mathcal L_X(v)s$ satisfies
$$\gamma_K\kappa_{X,M}=R_h(\kappa_{Y,E})b.$$
Moreover $v$ is the actual diagram-site square mate on $\mathcal R_TK$, and its evaluation at $n$ is the $Q_n$-tensor square mate under the indicated comparisons. If the $Q_{W,n}$ are quotient ring sheaves in degree zero, this is the ordinary quotient-ring coefficient mate after restriction of scalars. These are equations of strict derived-tower morphisms and their derived limits. No completeness of $K$, reflector property of $C_W$, cartesianness or geometric finiteness is assumed.

proof.text: Work in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W)))$ using the small diagram-site realization. Write $i_{W,Z}:\Delta_WZ\to\mathcal R_WZ$ for tensoring with the strict augmentation, $j_{W,Z}:Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_W\Delta_WZ$ for the canonical constant-tower map, and $\chi_{u,Z}:\Delta R_uZ\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr R_u\Delta Z$ for the normalized constant-tower/direct-image comparison. Thus $\kappa_{W,Z}=\mathcal L_W(i_{W,Z})j_{W,Z}$. The evaluation comparisons carry the tower adjunction counits to the ambient ones and commute with transitions. Tensor and pullback comparisons here are constructed on the diagram site, so they give actual derived tower maps. Constant pullback commutes with $\Delta$ exactly; the stated counit equation for $\chi$ identifies the mate on constant towers with the constant tower of the ambient mate, by the defining transpose formula.

Under these normalized evaluation comparisons, $H_n$ is $L_f$ of $\pi_{g,K,Q_{S,n}}$ followed by the pullback/tensor identifications, and $H'_n$ is $\pi_{h,E,Q_{X,n}}$ followed by the corresponding identification with the $e$-pullback of the coefficient-tensored input. The new general ringed-site perfect projection theorem makes each of these maps invertible. The pulled-back $Q_{X,n}$ is perfect: on each object of a covering of $S$ over which $Q_{S,n}$ has a bounded summand-of-finite-free representative, the strict-perfect pullback model gives the termwise pulled-back package with the same ranks and identifies $L_f$ of the representative with it; the inverse images of these covering objects cover the final sheaf of $X$, so every object of $X$ has a covering by objects over which $Q_{X,n}$ has such a representative. The same holds for the pullbacks to $T$ and $Y$. Hence $H,H'$ are invertible as derived tower maps. Indeed their cones have zero cohomology after every evaluation; levelwise kernels and cokernels show that each cohomology tower is zero, so the cones are acyclic. This only uses detection of isomorphisms, not detection of equality of morphisms.

proof.text:
Apply the ringed exchange/tensor coherence theorem on the four diagram topoi, with input $\Delta_TK$ and coefficient $Q_{S,\bullet}$. It applies to this commutative ringed square without cartesianness and does not require the coefficient diagram to be perfect as a single diagram-site object. Let $\beta:B\to D$ be the diagram-site square mate on $\mathcal R_TK$. The theorem, together with the constant-tower mate comparison of Step 1, gives the equality of derived tower morphisms
$$\beta H=H'\mathcal R_X(b).$$
Here $\Delta_TK\otimes^L\mathscr L_gQ_{S,\bullet}=\mathcal R_TK$ and the analogous identifications on $X,Y$ are precisely the canonical tensor reassociations already specified in the question. Cancel $H$ to obtain $\beta=H'\mathcal R_X(b)H^{-1}=v$. This proves the tower equality directly on the diagram topoi.

Evaluate this actual mate using the counit-preserving evaluation comparisons. Its transpose is the evaluated pullback-square comparison followed by the evaluated $g$-counit; these are exactly the ordinary square comparison and counit on $K\otimes^LQ_{T,n}$. Thus $v_n$ is the $Q_n$-tensor square mate. When $Q_{W,n}$ are quotient ring sheaves, use the exact scalar-restriction functors and the normalized diagram-ring restriction/direct-image comparison. Apply the ringed comparison/tensor/adjunction theorem to the two paths from $(Y,Q_{Y,n})$ to $(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and similarly for $g$. Its composite counit equation identifies scalar restriction of the quotient adjunction counit with the ambient one after the inverse-image restriction comparison. Both geometric pullbacks are exact inverse image because both sets of coefficient rings are identified under inverse image. On inverse-image tensors the square comparisons send $x\otimes q$ to the inverse image of $x$ tensored with the inverse image of $q$ along either path. Therefore they agree. In the mate word (unit, square, counit), substitute these adjunction-compatible comparisons: it becomes the ambient evaluated mate. Hence the restricted quotient-ring mate equals $v_n$ under the specified comparisons; no fullness or faithfulness of derived scalar restriction is used.

The projection map is natural in the coefficient object and is the identity on the tensor unit. Apply this to the actual diagram-site coefficient map $a_X:\Delta\mathcal O_X[0]\to Q_{X,\bullet}$. After the normalized constant-tower identifications, its naturality square is the equality
$$H'i_{X,N}=\mathscr R_h(i_{Y,E})\chi_{h,E}:\Delta_XN\longrightarrow D.$$
The map at the unit is $\chi_{h,E}$: its transpose is the tower counit, since the counit equation for $\chi$ identifies it with the constant ambient counit. The coefficient map pulled to $Y$ is exactly the given strict augmentation there. The pullback/tensor reassociation in $H'$ carries it to $i_{Y,E}$ by naturality. This proves the equation in the tower derived category before taking limits.

Put $a_Z=a_{h,Z}:R_h\mathcal L_YZ\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_X\mathscr R_hZ$ for the canonical natural direct-image/limit comparison, so $c=a_{\mathcal R_YE}$. Naturality at $i_{Y,E}$ gives
$$c\,R_h\mathcal L_Y(i_{Y,E})=\mathcal L_X\mathscr R_h(i_{Y,E})\,a_{\Delta_YE}.$$
Constant-tower normalization gives
$$a_{\Delta_YE}R_h(j_{Y,E})=\mathcal L_X(\chi_{h,E})j_{X,N}.$$
The latter is the normalized identity $\mathcal L_X(\chi)^{-1}a_{\Delta}=1$ expressed using $j$ at the two corners. Apply $\mathcal L_X$ to Step 5 and use these two equations. After composing with $j_{X,N}$ and then cancelling $c$, obtain
$$c^{-1}\mathcal L_X(H')\kappa_{X,N}=R_h(\kappa_{Y,E}).$$
All comparisons used are the derived-composite comparisons, so equality is not being inferred from tower projections.

Naturality of tensoring the strict augmentation gives $\mathcal R_X(b)i_{X,M}=i_{X,N}\Delta_X(b)$. The constant-tower map $j$ is natural, being the inverse of the canonical natural identification $\mathcal L_X\Delta_X\cong\mathrm{id}$. Thus functoriality gives
$$\mathcal L_X\mathcal R_X(b)\kappa_{X,M}=\kappa_{X,N}b.$$
Using $s=\mathcal L_XH$ and $vH=H'\mathcal R_X(b)$, now calculate
$$\begin{aligned}
\gamma_K\kappa_{X,M}
&=c^{-1}\mathcal L_X(v)\mathcal L_X(H)\kappa_{X,M}\\
&=c^{-1}\mathcal L_X(H')\mathcal L_X\mathcal R_X(b)\kappa_{X,M}\\
&=c^{-1}\mathcal L_X(H')\kappa_{X,N}b
=R_h(\kappa_{Y,E})b.
\end{aligned}$$
Naturality in $K$ follows from the naturality of the adjunction mate, projection maps, augmentation, and limit comparisons used throughout. No invertibility of $b$ or $\kappa$ was used.
